builds.howItPlays: You fight over battlefields with cheap units and swing those fights with cards like Spinning Axe, a piece of gear you can play even in the middle of a fight that attaches to a unit and gives it +3 Might. Every combat you win, attacking or defending, draws you a card as long as one of your units survives, and Draven, Showboat grows stronger with every point you score.
builds.whyYou: You like combat math and want every fight to be a real decision: which unit gets the Axe, what you keep face down, and what your opponent can still answer with. You're happy to trade blows for a few turns, knowing each fight you win refills your hand and each point you score makes Showboat scarier. You accept that some fast decks will run you over if you fall behind early. If you'd rather out-think an opponent one combat at a time than race them, Draven gives you plenty to chew on.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 5: the hextech guide says to 'use cheap units to establish the first battlefield', but Showboat only becomes a threat as your points climb, and riftbound.gg says he needs 4 points to matter and the deck struggles when behind. That is a middle-game plan, level with Jax (5/6/7/5.5) and Kha'Zix (5/6/7/6.5). stance 5.5 (was 4): hextech's legend guide calls the deck proactive, and the Legend draws on any combat win, attacking or defending, if a friendly unit survives. The RQ lists attack with Noxus Hopeful, Kai'Sa and Evelynn's pull, but they also run defensive tools: Overzealous Fan returns an attacker to base, Tideturner swaps from Hidden, and 2-3 Rebuke. That puts the deck a little under the proactive Midrange Builds (Akali 6, Jax 6) and above reactive Leona (3). complexity 7: hextech walks through Quick-Draw timing, Hidden setup at controlled battlefields, and sacrificing Fan while keeping a second defender. Kept level with Jax and Kha'Zix at 7. variance 6.5: Hidden cards and cards played mid-combat decide fights, and hextech Snapshot #7 says the engine needs an actual fight and the deck is less self-sufficient during setup. Losing Stacked Deck's card selection keeps variance from dropping, level with Kha'Zix 6.5 and below LeBlanc 7. Legend ability: when you win a combat, draw 1 card (a friendly unit must survive). Confidence: high on the label, medium on the coordinates. Change 2026-09-23: stance moved from 4 to 5.5. The old reading leaned on riftbound.gg's 'a control, reactive environment' line, which can be read as the field Draven does well in rather than how Draven plays, and hextech calls the deck proactive. The budget Miracle variant behind the old variance and label notes shows up in no top list after the March ban. The other axes and the label are unchanged. hextech's legend page leans toward calling the deck aggressive and tempo-focused, but riftbound.gg, riftbound.zone and the RQ lists agree on Midrange, so the label stays.
